newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India sells 50,000/T Dec Bombay naphtha to Vitol.
newsitem.headline: India sells 50,000/T Dec Bombay naphtha to Vitol.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has sold by tender 50,000 tonnes of December naphtha from Bombay on the west coast to Dutch trader Vitol on Japanese related prices, industry sources said on Friday.

One cargo of 25,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) lifting December 5-7 was awarded at a discount of $20.10 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board basis, and the other 25,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha (LAN) lifting December 10-12 at a discount of $17.35 a tonne.
Both tenders closed November 28 and were valid until November 29.
Traders said the cargoes were sold on a price linked to Japanese prices due to the strong demand in North Asia.
The steep one-month backwardation of around $5.00/$5.50 a tonne in the forward open-specification contract from first-half February reflected this strength, traders said.

In its last tender, IOC sold 30,000 tonnes of HAN lifting November 20-22 to Dutch trader Vitol at $36.63 a tonne below U.S. Gulf quotes spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis from Cochin, industry sources said on Wednesday.
IOC sold its last LAN cargo to Swiss trader Glencore at $28.72 a tonne below Northwest European quotes, fob Vizag lifting November 24-26.
